obligation_matrix.negative_test: Mutate the attempt-ledger prefix or leave a marker without its directory, force recovery exit 1, and record the forensic hold: after restart every prepare/authorize/publish/recover/supersede mode rejects before opening a key; deleting, mutating, duplicating, or forging the hold does not restore progress; fault injection at every fsync/rename/lock boundary yields only closed recovery states.
obligation_matrix.exit_criterion: All attempt-machine, fault-injection, and forensic-hold fixtures in Task 12 Step 3 pass; exactly one PUBLISHED attempt exists, superseded attempts are preserved, and hold enforcement survives restart.

obligation_matrix.invariant: Runtime code is ESM on Node 18 and 20, uses only node: and repository-relative imports, adds zero dependencies, performs no external network, and is portable to a neutral fresh host without authority or institutional-memory files; missing host adapters block explicitly rather than invoking TELOS defaults.
obligation_matrix.mechanism: `test-production-import-policy.mjs` tokenizes JS, derives its seed inventory mechanically from every Create:/Modify: executable row of the matured plan plus recursive directory walks, audits the transitive relative-import closure, and rejects nonliteral/external targets; `test-production-fresh-host.mjs` copies only build-gate/merkle-dag runtime into a neutral-named temporary host with no CURRENT-AUTHORITY.json or institutional memory; binding Node 18/20 CI matrix.
obligation_matrix.negative_test: Hidden nonliteral/external import mutations (comments, strings, templates, escapes, dynamic expressions, require()) fail the audit; the fresh host compiles a minimal profile, then removal of one triggered adapter returns the exact typed blocker without reading any TELOS authority or institutional-memory file.
obligation_matrix.exit_criterion: Both proof scripts pass on every Node 18 and 20 CI leg with the plan-derived seed-set equality proven; no dependency or lockfile addition exists in build-gate/merkle-dag.

obligation_matrix.invariant: Governance and acceptance evidence are independently re-derived from exact committed bytes and strict Git ancestry; the live parallel workshop has two distinct source parents and an exact 29-row bijection; authorization, Argo, self-hosting, docs, Clotho, post-review, retrospective, lifecycle verification, enrollment, and binding Node 18/20 evidence retain their prescribed order; producer status strings never authorize or prove acceptance.
obligation_matrix.mechanism: Task 13 institutional oracle verifies mode live, exactly two constraints/implementation source parents with re-hashed response artifacts, `descends_from` equal to exactly those two refs, and an exact PPC-W01–PPC-W29 29-row six-field bijection; strict ancestry chain post_review < retrospective < lifecycle_verification < enrollment with commands independently re-run; Task 14 acceptance verifier (revised to exactly --verify-local/--verify-ci) derives every predicate itself, treating asserted statuses as assertions only; --verify-ci binds GITHUB_SHA, strict ancestry, and the exact runtime major per matrix leg.
obligation_matrix.negative_test: Mutation corpus: delete/duplicate/rename one matrix row or change one row's five-field tuple, stale-bind or remove one source parent, delete a required Argo slice event, place enrollment in the post-review/retrospective commit, and flip every asserted status to pass while one evidence ref/command/result is stale — the institutional and acceptance oracles reject each independently of signatures and status text.
obligation_matrix.exit_criterion: test-production-profile-contract.mjs and test-production-profile-acceptance.mjs --self-test pass their complete mutation corpora; the default oracle proves the bijection, distinct parentage, and strict ancestry on the enrolled commit; both CI matrix legs independently re-derive acceptance.

conflicts: The closed authority-anchor set is not preserved in the integrated plan. Global Constraints retains the approved-design raw SHA-256, but replaces the Iliad pre-review raw SHA-256 `7b96f60ab9280c8c8173723f30892f4104583f5c9db17c44877bc724507ab634` with paths and abbreviated commit `git:6bb0d5f`, and omits the binding Daedalus-methodology SHA-256 `9288e17e84b202e48c4dbfad13904abc9317bae22b82aeefa01ee6b837a0c406` and frozen-candidate SHA-256 `67de2ff93499b036a35964014a5222a504ca57c9c1f9fed6fcb9fa4f9b6b210b`. Later lineage checks do not supply predicates requiring equality to those three frozen byte hashes, so stale or substituted anchor bytes are not excluded by the matured plan itself.

Task 1's atomic-write mechanism does not satisfy the absolute nonzero-output preservation contract. It performs rename before the final parent-directory fsync and reports success only after that fsync. Therefore an injected post-rename parent-fsync failure produces a cannot-run invocation after the previously valid output may already have been replaced by complete new bytes. No rollback, indeterminate-commit protocol, or predicate reconciling this state is specified, conflicting with PPC-W23 and the global rule that a failed invocation never replaces a previously valid output.

The finding-code jurisdictions are contradictory. Task 10 requires every externally visible `finding_code`, explicitly including demo/self-publication and institutional fixtures, to belong to Task 1's 20 compiler codes. Task 12 then defines the forensic-hold `finding_code` vocabulary as `LEDGER_PREFIX_MISMATCH`, `PUBLICATION_BYTES_MISMATCH`, `MARKER_WITHOUT_DIRECTORY`, `LOCK_STATE_UNSAFE`, and `RECOVERY_STATE_UNSAFE`, none of which is in that compiler set. The source contract permits a separately closed publication/recovery diagnostic vocabulary; the integrated cross-surface membership sweep both removes that separation and is unsatisfiable with Task 12.

PPC-W27's durable forensic-hold transition is not atomic with unsafe recovery. `--recover-publication` is specified to exit `1` for an unsafe state, after which a shell wrapper separately invokes `--record-forensic-hold`. A crash, signal, or process loss between those commands leaves a completed unsafe recovery result without the required durable signed hold, allowing a subsequent process to encounter no hold. The prose assertion that recovery exit 1 is made durable before process exit is not implemented by this two-process sequence; the recovery mode already receives the governance key and must itself install and fsync the hold before returning exit 1, or use an equivalent single durable transition.
